raw_response:
I'm 62 years old, been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Me and my husband manage everything ourselves. We're getting on in years, so we have to be careful with money and with our backs. Can't hire help — too expensive for a small farm like ours.

The wheat went in last October like always. I used the hybrid seed I've trusted for years, about 15 jin per mu. When I sowed, I put down base fertilizer — compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 50 jin per mu. That gives me a bit of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all together. Then in March when the wheat greened up, I topdressed with about 25 jin of urea per mu. Now it's April, and if the wheat looks a little yellow at jointing, I'll add another 15 jin of urea. The extension agent says 20 kg nitrogen per mu is the target, but I've tried more and I've tried less. On my land, around 14 kg total nitrogen is the sweet spot. I get about 420 kg per mu of wheat, which is enough for our needs. More fertilizer just costs more money and means more heavy bags to carry, for yield that might not even pay for itself. I irrigate the wheat three times — once after planting, once at green-up, and once more before heading if there's no rain. Water from the tube well isn't free anymore with the meters, so I watch it, but you can't let wheat go thirsty at heading stage. I spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide. Come early June, I hire a combine to harvest — about 50 yuan per mu. We're too old to cut 6 mu by hand.

The summer maize gets planted right after the wheat comes off in early June. Sometimes we only have 3–5 days, so there's no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed from the agricultural supply shop, about 3–4 jin per mu, costs about 45 yuan per mu. I plant directly into the wheat stubble with my small planter — no time for deep tillage. At planting I put down about 50 jin per mu of compound fertilizer. Then in mid-July at the big-flare stage, I topdress with about 20 jin of urea. Total nitrogen comes to about 12 kg per mu. The extension people say do 18 kg, but honestly, I did 12 kg two years ago and 15 kg last year, and the yield difference on my land wasn't worth the extra cost. I expect around 480 kg per mu if the summer rains are decent. For maize, I figure on irrigating once or twice — usually at planting if the soil is dry, and once at tasseling in August if the rains don't come. Some years I don't need to irrigate maize at all, but I always plan for at least one. I spray herbicide right after planting.

For labor, it's just us two. The wheat season takes about 12 days of our work spread across the year — planting, fertilizing, irrigating, spraying, and keeping an eye on things. Maize takes about 10 days. We don't hire day laborers — can't afford it. The combine is the only outside help, and that's a machine, not people.

My total costs run about 2,700 yuan for both crops. It's a big chunk for a small farm like ours, but you have to spend money to make money. I'd rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing half your crop hurts a lot more than saving a few hundred yuan.
